text: This is a housekeeping step rather than a new feature: the agent is simplifying the Rust port's code and updating the project's public notes to record what has been merged so far. It matters because a leaner, better-documented codebase is easier to keep extending one verified step at a time as the port chases feature parity with the original. It comes at a moment when the Rust version is faster in three of the seven measured scenarios, slower in three and level in one, with the widest gap on real-world projects, where it takes about 1.46 times as long on a fresh copy and about 1.66 times as long when nothing has changed.
